_comment: Material / surface treatments. A treatment re-steps a base's OWN body cells by a deterministic rule -- it adds no geometry and invents no colour, so it composes freely with every palette and every shape. That is why it is a separate axis from the decal system rather than a kind of decal: a plaid covers the whole crown, which no zone-bounded piece can express.

rules.speckle: a deterministic hash of (x,y) lifts `density` of eligible cells by `delta` steps
rules.check: every `period`-th column and every `row_period`-th row lift by `delta`; crossings lift twice
rules.panel: one horizontal seam row and one vertical centre seam drop by `delta`

felt.label: felt
felt.note: the plain material, and the commonest in the reference

wool.label: brushed wool
wool.note: scattered lighter flecks, as on the tan and dusty-pink references

plaid.label: plaid check
plaid.note: the pale cross-hatch on the light blue reference

min_step_note: min_step keeps a treatment off the rim and shade steps (2 and 3). Those carry the hat's construction -- its edge and its round -- and texturing them turns a readable silhouette into noise at 16px. With a flat step-4 body the material has the whole crown to work on and needs nothing below it.
